title: Eliminating Centralized Latency and costs with Peer to Peer In-Band...
content: Eliminating Centralized Latency and costs with Peer to Peer In-Band Identity Note Why AgentDNAAs AI agents transition from passive assistants to autonomous actors, we will see significant elevation in security, accountability and cross-domain interoperability risks. Current OAuth-based systems and static policy-based access management rules are designed for human-focused sessions, failing to address the complexities of agentic delegation and long-lived non-human identities. To bridge this gap, we built AgentDNA, a novel AI security framework that shifts the paradigm from stateless, token-based (Proof of Possession) authentication to a stateful Chain of Custody authentication (CoCA) - a construct we introduce to codify the continuous, verifiable link between human intent and machine action. AgentDNA framework also introduces Context-Based Access Management (CBAC), transforming access management from role-based or policy-based static rules into a dynamic, reasoning-aware process. Finally, we address the critical requirement for immutable logs. This persistent, immutable audit trail is essential for forensic accountability, providing a definitive record that prevents alteration of execution history.AgentDNA not only addresses the key security risks in Agentic IAM, but also solves the key operational challenges less discussed – scale and latency. Existing centralized IdPs will fall significantly short of the latency requirements for Agentic Auth. Further, the additional infrastructure costs for meeting the Agentic Auth are prohibitively high. We estimate that to handle one billion Agentic auth instructions per minute will cost an additional US$10.5 billion in infra costs alone. It is worth noting that the CEO of one of the largest security companies in the world noted that we may need to resolve 60 billion Agentic transactions per minute, 60x the assumptions we have used. AgentDNA p2p technology, however, will require less than US$1 million in additional infrastructure costs. The latency is also 340x better compared to the centralized IdP solutions. Let us explain more on the scale, cost and latency advantages of AgentDNA.

title: Product Note Scale, cost and latency: AgentDNA vs Centralized IdPTraditional...
content:
Product Note Scale, cost and latency: AgentDNA vs Centralized IdPTraditional identity architectures rely on synchronous, out-of-band calls to a centralized IdP. In a multi-agent mesh, this creates a compounding latency that disproportionately affects the tail end of your performance distribution. By moving to In-Band Auth, AgentDNA secures the execution flow at the peer to peer (P2P) level.N+1 Round Trip Latency: In a workflow of N agents, a centralized model requires N round trips to an IdP for token exchange. With Chain of Custody Authentication (CoCA), verification is a local, CPU bound operation rather than a network bound operation.HandShake Delay: Traditional OAuth/OIDC flows require a Handshake Warm-up (TCP/TLS setup + Metadata discovery + Token exchange). The Auth-to-Work ratio for a short lived agent is very high. The handshake period with AgentDNA is Zero aince agents verify the incoming task and start processing in the same clock cycle making Micro Agents viable for high-frequency security operations.

title: Product Note Centralised IdP vs Peer to Peer Infrastructure For...
content:
Product Note Centralised IdP vs Peer to Peer Infrastructure For an IdP to handle 1 billion agent auth transactions, it would need to build a Hyperscale Auth Layer. If 1 billion agents perform just one auth action per minute, the IdP must handle ~16.7 million Requests Per Second (RPS). Today's IdPs (Okta/Auth0) max out at 1,500 RPS in a single private cloud instance. To support 16.7 million RPS with sub 100ms latency, the IdP would need thousands of global clusters, massive caching layers. Therefore, the IdP will charge for SLA guarantee with a risk premium since it is now a Single Point of Failure for one billion agents and its insurance and liability costs skyrocket. By using AgentDNA Peer to Peer CoCA architecture, the external service fee is eliminated as the agent owner already possesses the computational resource. In a network of 1 billion agents, 50,000 to 100,000 vCPUs are likely required to run the tasks. vCPU additional costs for AgentDNA will be a fraction of this.

title: Enterprise Grade Identity Management and Governance Infrastructure for Agents Executive...
content:
Enterprise Grade Identity Management and Governance Infrastructure for Agents Executive Summary: AgentDNA is the first unified framework designed to close the "Agent Gap" - the security vacuum created when autonomous AI agents act on behalf of users. It provides a verifiable bridge between human intent and machine execution.
Product Note IAM and Governance Crisis in Agentic World The Delegation Risk: Legacy IAM protocols like OAuth¹ and SAML² use long-lived session tokens built for human login - not agent delegation.Privilege Mirroring: Agents are new entities at Service Provider layer, inserting full user permissions violating the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP). Auditability : Standard logs are modifiable and hence offer Zero Security Value during audit. Sybil Attack: A rogue service can spawn thousands of headless agents that appear as legitimate, unique actors within a network, bypassing traditional security The AgentDNA Solution: A Unified Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Autonomous Governance Framework for Agentic AI1. Chain of Custody Authentication (CoCA) Beyond Proof of Possession: Shifts security from session based "who has the token" to intent based "how was this action derived." Recursive Envelope: Every sub-agent call is wrapped in a signature chain (User - Primary Agent - Sub-Agent). If the chain breaks, authentication fails2. Context-Based Access Control (CBAC) Dynamic Trust Scoring: Moves beyond static RBAC³ / ABAC⁴ models. Permissions are granted and revoked in real time based on execution context, behaviour, and risk.¹ OAuth: User-consent authorization for apps; not designed for autonomous agents.² SAML: Enterprise SSO protocol with static trust and session³ RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): Access decisions are based on predefined roles with static permissions.⁴ ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control): Access is evaluated using fixed attributes of the subject, resource, and environment.
